conventions.code_verification: ontoserver_only: SNOMED CT or LOINC code verified on the CSIRO Ontoserver on 2026-11-13. synthea_module+ontoserver: also emitted by Synthea. icd10_observed_in_loaded_data: ICD-10 code seen in the loaded data (ICD-10 is not served by that terminology server).

owner_decisions.summary: The NP-NCD operational guidelines 2023 to 2030 are the current programme document and confirm the scope (adults 30 and above, five conditions) but state no screening intervals and no upper age. Intervals, methods and the 30 to 65 band come from the MoHFW operational guidelines (June 2016) and Operational Framework (Aug 2016), repeated in NHM training modules. It is not verified that later instructions leave them unchanged.

Hypertension and diabetes: 30 and above, no upper age. Cancers: 30 to 65 as in the programme table (repeated in three documents); the prose of the same documents says 'over 30'. Residents over 65 are not_eligible with reason above_age_65_programme_band for the three cancers.
Breast and cervical screening are for 'all women'. Sex assigned at birth female is the proxy (limitation shared with D-11 of the US pack). Oral, hypertension and diabetes do not use sex.

Hypertension: any recorded blood pressure. Diabetes: any recorded glucose (random, fasting, capillary); HbA1c is NOT counted. Breast: clinical breast examination, plus screening mammography counted as equivalent (not stated in the source). Cervical: VIA, plus Pap or HPV test counted as equivalent (the Framework allows Pap where available but gives no Pap interval). Oral: oral visual examination only.

A documented diagnosis of the condition (hypertension, diabetes, oral, breast or cervical cancer) gives not_eligible with a reason code naming the management or cancer care pathway. This is an engineering inference: the source follows known cases separately but never says 'exclude from screening'. Prediabetes is not known diabetes.

Hysterectomy (cervical) and bilateral mastectomy (breast) are not in the cited Indian guidance and route to requires_clinical_review instead of excluding automatically (same approach as D-09 of the US pack).

Menstruation and within 12 weeks of delivery or abortion (cervical), tobacco, areca nut or alcohol users below 30 (oral), the CBAC risk score (explicitly 'not a point of elimination'), symptomatic individuals (screened at any time), VIA positive follow up at one year, and referral thresholds (blood pressure 140/90, random glucose 140 mg/dl: referral criteria, not eligibility; the engine does not compare observation values).

Synthea emits no clinical breast examination, oral examination or VIA records, so already_completed for those comes only from AI extracted evidence or planted data. Residents stored with the lean 'rules' profile lack blood pressure, glucose and condition records for these selectors: evaluate them only after re-ingesting with the full profile, otherwise they appear falsely eligible.

any_clinical_record_recent.description: Any accepted structured clinical record dated inside the coverage window. Used only by the record_coverage prerequisite (ASSUMPTION A-01, not from any guideline).
any_clinical_record_recent.note: coverage_lookback_years=5 is an engineering assumption (owner decision D-01 of the US draft), reused unchanged.

excerpts.location: Section iii (The Service Delivery Framework), para (iv), printed p. 8
excerpts.text: Screening for cancers will take place once in five years, and for hypertension and diabetes it should be done annually.

excerpts.location: Section iii, para (xv), printed p. 10
excerpts.text: The target population for screening is as follows: All men and women over 30 years for Oral Cancer, Hypertension and Diabetes Mellitus; All women over 30 years for Cervical and Breast Cancer

excerpts.location: Section v (Referral and Treatment), para (i), printed p. 12
excerpts.text: Those with a systolic BP of over 140 and a diastolic BP of over 90 mm of Hg, or random blood sugar of 140 mg/dl and above) would be referred to a Medical officer (MBBS), at the nearest facility, for confirmation, conducting relevant laboratory investigations, and initiation of treatment.

excerpts.location: Chapter 2, Table 1 (Method and Frequency of Screening), printed p. 3
excerpts.text: Hypertension: 30 years and above, blood pressure apparatus (digital or aneroid sphygmomanometer), once a year. Diabetes: 30 years and above, glucometer, once a year. Breast cancer: 30-65 years, Clinical Breast Examination (CBE), once in 5 years. Oral cancer: 30-65 years, Oral Visual Examination (OVE), once in 5 years. Cervical cancer: 30-65 years, Visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA), once in 5 years (at the level of PHC to start with).

excerpts.location: Chapter 2, printed p. 3
excerpts.text: Every individual will be screened annually for Hypertension (High Blood Pressure) and Diabetes. For common Cancers, the screening should be done once in 5 years.

excerpts.location: Chapter 6 (Cancers), Figure 3 oral cancer flowchart, printed p. 37
excerpts.text: Screen all adults 30 years of age and above and all individuals with history of tobacco/areca nut/alcohol habits irrespective of age

sources.publication_date_basis: cover reads 2023; the exact day is not stated, 1 January is a placeholder

sources.verification: excerpts matched against text extracted from the downloaded PDF; the text was searched for screening frequencies and an upper age and none are stated

excerpts.location: Chapter 4 (Operational strategies), PHC HWC, Screening, Population Based Screening, printed p. 23
excerpts.text: After screening persons aged 30 years and above for Hypertension, Diabetes, Oral Cancer, Breast Cancer and Cervical Cancer, COPD & Asthma, Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD), the CHO/ ANM/ MPW refers suspected cases to the PHC Medical Officer to identify those individuals who have NCDs and warranting them further investigations, management and counselling.

excerpts.location: Chapter 4, individual/family/community level, printed p. 20
excerpts.text: ASHA would administer Community Based Assessment Checklist (CBAC) for all individuals of 30 years and above age group in the population. Through CBAC administration, a scoring is done for individuals, which is not a point of elimination but a score of 4 or more implies high risk.

excerpts.location: Chapter 6 (Cancers), cervical cancer screening, printed p. 60
excerpts.text: Women who are 30 years of age and above should be screened by a trained provider- lady physician or staff nurse at least once in five years except in the following situations- menstruation, pregnancy, within 12 weeks of delivery/ abortion and previous history of treatment for Cancer of the Cervix.

excerpts.location: Chapter 1, Table 2 (Referral process after screening), printed p. 9
excerpts.text: Hypertension: systolic BP of over 140 and/or a diastolic BP of over 90 mm of Hg (140/90 mm Hg). Diabetes: random blood sugar over 140 mg/dl. First level of referral: Medical officer (MBBS) at the nearest facility, for confirmation, conducting relevant laboratory investigations.

rules.name: Record coverage prerequisite (engineering assumption)
rules.description: At least one accepted clinical record in the last 5 years must exist, otherwise the absence of screening or exclusion evidence says nothing.
rules.label: illustrative, pending clinical review

explanation_templates.false: No clinical record in the last 5 years, so the absence of screening or exclusion evidence says nothing and the resident cannot be assessed.
explanation_templates.unknown: No clinical record in the last 5 years, so the resident cannot be assessed.

rules.notes: The 5 year window is not from any guideline (owner decision D-01 of the US draft pack, reused).

explanation_templates.false: Under 30: the programme screens adults aged 30 and above.
explanation_templates.unknown: The date of birth is missing or too imprecise to decide whether the resident is old enough.

rules.name: Known hypertension
rules.label: illustrative, pending clinical review

explanation_templates.true: Known hypertension is documented: the resident follows the treatment and follow up pathway, not routine screening.
explanation_templates.unknown: A possible diagnosis of hypertension is recorded but not yet confirmed, so screening eligibility cannot be decided.

rules.notes: Engineering inference (owner decision D-IN-05): the programme registers known cases separately and follows them up with treatment, and screening is described for people not yet diagnosed. The text never says 'exclude from screening'.

rules.name: Blood pressure measured within 12 months
rules.label: illustrative, pending clinical review

explanation_templates.true: Blood pressure was measured within the last 12 months, so annual screening is up to date.
explanation_templates.unknown: A screening record exists but its date or status is uncertain, so it cannot be decided whether the resident is up to date.

indeterminate_conditions: A matching completion fact is uncertain or not yet accepted -> unknown -> insufficient_evidence
A matching completion fact exists but its date is missing or straddles the interval boundary -> unknown
No matching fact at all -> rule false (documented record semantics): 'no documented screening', never 'not done'
rules.notes: Any recorded blood pressure measurement counts as documented screening (setting not distinguished). Due date = last measurement + 1 year.

excerpts.text: Women who are 30 years of age and above should be screened by a trained provider- lady physician or staff nurse at least once in five years except in the following situations- menstruation, pregnancy, within 12 weeks of delivery/ abortion and previous history of treatment for Cancer of the Cervix.

excerpts.location: Chapter 2, Table 1 (Method and Frequency of Screening), printed p. 3
excerpts.text: Hypertension: 30 years and above, blood pressure apparatus (digital or aneroid sphygmomanometer), once a year. Diabetes: 30 years and above, glucometer, once a year. Breast cancer: 30-65 years, Clinical Breast Examination (CBE), once in 5 years. Oral cancer: 30-65 years, Oral Visual Examination (OVE), once in 5 years. Cervical cancer: 30-65 years, Visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA), once in 5 years (at the level of PHC to start with).

excerpts.location: Chapter 2, printed p. 3
excerpts.text: Every individual will be screened annually for Hypertension (High Blood Pressure) and Diabetes. For common Cancers, the screening should be done once in 5 years.

excerpts.text: After screening persons aged 30 years and above for Hypertension, Diabetes, Oral Cancer, Breast Cancer and Cervical Cancer, COPD & Asthma, Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD), the CHO/ ANM/ MPW refers suspected cases to the PHC Medical Officer to identify those individuals who have NCDs and warranting them further investigations, management and counselling.

excerpts.location: Chapter 4, individual/family/community level, printed p. 20
excerpts.text: ASHA would administer Community Based Assessment Checklist (CBAC) for all individuals of 30 years and above age group in the population. Through CBAC administration, a scoring is done for individuals, which is not a point of elimination but a score of 4 or more implies high risk.

decision_policy.name: precedence_v2
decision_policy.contribution: For each rule take outcome_by_expression_result[expression result]; null contributes nothing; a criterion error contributes evaluation_error. The overall outcome is the highest-ranked contribution; none -> eligible.
decision_policy.primary_reason: reason_code (or reason_code_when_unknown for an unknown result) of the contributing rule with the winning outcome and the lowest priority number

rules.name: Record coverage prerequisite (engineering assumption)
rules.description: At least one accepted clinical record in the last 5 years must exist, otherwise the absence of screening or exclusion evidence says nothing.
rules.label: illustrative, pending clinical review

explanation_templates.false: No clinical record in the last 5 years, so the absence of screening or exclusion evidence says nothing and the resident cannot be assessed.
explanation_templates.unknown: No clinical record in the last 5 years, so the resident cannot be assessed.

rules.notes: The 5 year window is not from any guideline (owner decision D-01 of the US draft pack, reused).

rules.name: Women only
rules.label: illustrative, pending clinical review

explanation_templates.false: The programme screens women for this cancer; sex assigned at birth is used as a proxy (a limitation, not a clinical statement).
explanation_templates.unknown: Sex assigned at birth is missing, so the resident cannot be matched to the programme population.

rules.notes: Sex assigned at birth female is a proxy for 'women' (same limitation as D-11 of the US draft pack).

explanation_templates.false: Under 30: the programme screens adults aged 30 and above.
explanation_templates.unknown: The date of birth is missing or too imprecise to decide whether the resident is old enough.

rules.name: Age 65 or under
rules.label: illustrative, pending clinical review

explanation_templates.false: Over 65: the programme schedule for this screening covers ages 30 to 65.
explanation_templates.unknown: The date of birth is missing or too imprecise to decide whether the resident is within the age band.

rules.notes: Upper age taken from the programme table (owner decision D-IN-02). The prose of the same documents says 'over 30'.

explanation_templates.true: Previous cervical cancer is documented: routine VIA screening does not apply (the programme lists previous treatment for cancer of the cervix as an exception).
explanation_templates.unknown: A possible cervical cancer is recorded but not yet confirmed, so screening eligibility cannot be decided.

rules.name: Hysterectomy documented
rules.label: illustrative, pending clinical review

explanation_templates.true: Hysterectomy documented: a clinician decides whether routine screening still applies.
explanation_templates.unknown: Hysterectomy documented is uncertain, so screening eligibility cannot be decided.

rules.notes: Not in the cited Indian guidance; routed to clinical review instead of excluding automatically (owner decision D-IN-06).

rules.name: Currently pregnant
rules.label: illustrative, pending clinical review

explanation_templates.true: Currently pregnant: VIA screening is deferred until after pregnancy.
explanation_templates.unknown: A possible pregnancy is recorded but not yet confirmed, so screening eligibility cannot be decided.

rules.notes: Menstruation and 'within 12 weeks of delivery or abortion' are also exceptions in the source but are not modelled (no deterministic data).

rules.name: Cervical screening within 5 years
rules.label: illustrative, pending clinical review

explanation_templates.true: A cervical screening test was done within the last 5 years, so screening is up to date.
explanation_templates.unknown: A screening record exists but its date or status is uncertain, so it cannot be decided whether the resident is up to date.

indeterminate_conditions: A matching completion fact is uncertain or not yet accepted -> unknown -> insufficient_evidence
A matching completion fact exists but its date is missing or straddles the interval boundary -> unknown
No matching fact at all -> rule false (documented record semantics): 'no documented screening', never 'not done'
rules.notes: VIA is the programme method; a Pap smear or HPV test within 5 years is counted as equivalent (owner decision D-IN-04) because the Framework allows Pap where available but gives no interval for it. Synthea has no VIA. Due date = last test + 5 years.
